The '''2014–15 Bundesliga''' was the 52nd season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[association football|football]] competition. The season started on 22 August 2014 and the final matchday took place on 23 May 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se15388/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2014/2015 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] won their 25th [[List of German football champions|German title]] on 26 April 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/32475479|title=Bayern Munich: Pep Guardiola's side win club's 25th German title|date=26 April 2015|access-date=23 August 2026|website=Bbc.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2015/apr/28/bayern-munich-bundesliga-pep-guardiola|title=Bayern Munich charge ahead to leave their German rivals playing catch-up|date=28 April 2015|website=Theguardian.com|access-date=28 April 2015}}</ref>

==Background==
Bayern Munich came into the season as defending champions, winning the championship on 25 March 2014 against [[Hertha BSC]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Der FC Bayern feiert die erste März-Meisterschaft|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/hertha-bsc/article126177497/Der-FC-Bayern-feiert-die-erste-Maerz-Meisterschaft.html|access-date=22 May 2014|newspaper=Die Welt|date=25 March 2014|language=de}}</ref> [[Armin Veh]] announced that he was leaving [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] during the [[2013–14 Eintracht Frankfurt season|2013–14 season]].<ref name=vehresigned/> He had demanded that the club invest more money in the squad.<ref>{{cite news|title=Trainer Veh bereitet in Frankfurt seinen Abgang vor|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/eintracht-frankfurt/article114478144/Trainer-Veh-bereitet-in-Frankfurt-seinen-Abgang-vor.html|access-date=22 May 2014|newspaper=[[Die Welt]]|date=15 March 2014|language=de}}</ref> [[Thomas Schaaf]] replaced Veh.<ref name="Der ewige Bremer wird Frankfurter"/>

[[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] sacked [[Sami Hyypiä]] during the [[2013–14 Bayer 04 Leverkusen season|2013–14 season]].<ref name="Leverkusen trennt sich von Trainer Hyypiä"/> [[Sascha Lewandowski]] was named interim manager.<ref name="Leverkusen trennt sich von Trainer Hyypiä"/> Lewandowski's interim reign lasted until the end of the season when [[Roger Schmidt (football manager)|Roger Schmidt]] took over.<ref name="Bayer Leverkusen name Roger Schmidt as Sami Hyypia replacement"/> Other managerial changes include [[Kasper Hjulmand]]<ref name="Hjulmand übernimmt Tuchels Job"/> replacing [[Thomas Tuchel]]<ref name="Mainz-Manager Heidel: Trainer Tuchel will zurücktreten"/> at [[1. FSV Mainz 05]] and Armin Veh<ref name="returnVfB"/> replacing [[Huub Stevens]] at [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref name="Huub Stevens verlässt den VfB"/> Every club received their licence.<ref>{{cite news|title=DFL erteilt allen Klubs die Lizenz|url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/bundesliga-dfl-erteilt-allen-klubs-die-lizenz-1.1977060|access-date=29 May 2014|newspaper=Süddeutsche Zeitung|date=27 May 2014|language=de}}</ref> The league schedule came out on 24 June with [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] facing [[VfL Wolfsburg]] in the opening fixture on 22 August.<ref name="FC Bayern eröffnet Saison gegen Wolfsburg">{{cite news|title=FC Bayern eröffnet Saison gegen Wolfsburg|url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/bundesliga-fc-bayern-eroeffnet-saison-gegen-wolfsburg-1.2014038|access-date=18 July 2014|publisher=Süddeutsche Zeitung|date=24 June 2014|language=de}}</ref> The match ended 2–1 win for Bayern Munich, a record third straight win for the home team, on the opening matchday, in the last three seasons.

18 teams comprise the league. 15 sides qualified directly from the [[2013–14 Bundesliga|2013–14 season]] and two sides were directly promoted from the [[2013–14 2. Bundesliga|2013–14 2. Fußball-Bundesliga season]]: [[1. FC Köln]] and [[SC Paderborn 07]]. The final participant was decided by a [[2013–14 Bundesliga#Relegation play-offs|two-legged play-off]], in which 16th-placed Bundesliga club [[Hamburger SV]] defeated third-place finisher in [[2. Bundesliga]], [[SpVgg Greuther Fürth]].

==Relegation play-offs==
The team which finishes 16th, will face the third-placed [[2014–15 2. Bundesliga]] side for a two-legged play-off. The winner on [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] score after both matches earns entry into the [[2015–16 Bundesliga]]. [[Hamburger SV]] prevailed for the second year in a row, avoiding their possible first relegation.
